A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Jet-Nemotron/PostNAS research. All 20 pages of each version, including figures, tables and Appendices A–B, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original architecture-search experiments, benchmark evaluations, throughput measurements and a controlled training-data study, including results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a comparison with two Falcon-H1 models in Appendix B.3 and Table 16.

M1.justification: The four-stage PostNAS procedure, JetBlock design, training objectives and Jet-Nemotron architectures remain unchanged in Sections 2–3.1 and Appendix A.1. The added Falcon-H1 discussion describes a comparator, not a modification to the proposed method.

E1.justification: The training corpora, six evaluation domains, context-length scenarios and hardware coverage are retained. Table 16 compares additional models on existing tasks; the Orin and RTX 3090 experiments already appear in v1.

E2.justification: Appendix B.3 and Table 16 add Falcon-H1-1.5B and Falcon-H1-1.5B-deep as evaluated comparators against both Jet-Nemotron models. Comparator membership in the existing experiments remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 13 revises reported prefilling chunk sizes: Qwen2.5-1.5B changes from 4,096 to 8,192, Qwen3-1.7B from 4,096 to 16,384, Jet-Nemotron-2B from 1,024 to 2,048, and Jet-Nemotron-4B from 512 to 1,024. Batch sizes remain unchanged. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish that measurements were rerun.

E4.justification: The component studies, layer-placement analysis, architecture-parameter search, context-length analysis and controlled training-data experiment are unchanged. The new Falcon-H1 table supplies benchmark comparisons, without an additional ablation or controlled test of the proposed efficiency explanation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for these evaluations. The added comparison continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 16 adds Falcon-H1 results across six accuracy columns and generation throughputs of 223 and 66 tokens/s for the standard and deep variants. Its Jet-Nemotron rows repeat existing results, including 2,885 and 1,271 tokens/s. Existing accuracy and throughput scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, assumptions, proofs or derivations are added or revised. Section 3.3 retains the same 14 × 4 = 56 theoretical speedup argument. The new Falcon-H1 mechanism discussion is qualitative.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list and conclusion retain the same PostNAS and JetBlock novelty claims and broad accuracy–efficiency claims, including the maximum 53.6× generation speedup. The added comparison supports the existing contribution rather than redefining it.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 newly attributes Falcon-H1’s lower throughput to sequential Mamba2/full-attention computation and the deep variant’s greater depth. Section 3.2 also softens the coding interpretation from higher average accuracy than all baselines to performance comparable with Qwen3-1.7B-Base; Table 7 retains averages of 59.5 and 58.9, respectively.

D1.justification: Table 13 revises the documented throughput hyperparameters. Table 3 also corrects the listed parameter count for Llama3.2-3B from 1.0B to 3.0B, without changing its identity or performance scores. Architecture details, training costs, software and hardware descriptions, and the code-access link otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Falcon-H1 as reference 106 and positions Jet-Nemotron’s layer-wise hybrid architecture against Falcon-H1’s head-wise approach in Appendix B.3. The existing references and main related-work discussion are retained.

P1.justification: v3 adds a short Appendix B.3 and makes localized edits to the coding-results paragraph, results summary, section-heading punctuation and running-header spacing. The document’s overall organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 16 and moves the unchanged Table 15 from the middle to the top of the final page to accommodate the comparison. Existing figures and table structures are retained, with only minor spacing adjustments elsewhere.

improvement.justification: The Falcon-H1 comparison adds relevant evidence against a concurrent hybrid-model family, and correcting Llama3.2-3B’s parameter count removes a misleading comparison detail. The coding discussion is also more cautious about a small accuracy difference. These are limited gains: the central method and results are unchanged, the new efficiency explanation lacks a controlled test, and the chunk-size revisions do not clarify whether measurements were rerun.
